summary:
22 Oct 2026 radar. I checked 9 of the leads below with WebSearch or WebFetch. Two new stories fit our winning lanes.

(1) Lane B, gray market: on Oct 21 CBS News published lab tests of vials sold as retatrutide and called the results "pretty terrifying". Our search couldn't find that quote; it comes from the feed headline. The same week, the Penn analysis of Reddit retatrutide posts was published in JAMA Network Open and reached ScienceDaily. Its most-reported symptom was increased appetite, but the authors say they can't link it to the drug or confirm what people actually took. This is the freshest hook for the "What's Actually Confirmed?" long-form.

(2) Lane C, first explainer: phase 3 results for retatrutide in sleep apnea were presented at Sleep Europe 2026 and are in NEJM. Apnea events per hour fell by about 32–34 on retatrutide versus about 10 on placebo. MedPage covered it on Oct 21, and there are almost no creator explainers yet. Put the new name first and use it within 48 hours.

Two Lane A search topics have high ad-value timing:
- Medicare open enrollment runs Oct 15 to Dec 7, and the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge has a $50 copay. Older US viewers pay well in ad rates.
- Thanksgiving eating on a GLP-1 will peak in mid to late November, and UC Davis Health has already published a guide.

There's also a myth-correction chance. A MassLive headline ("Mounjaro, Zepbound ingredient risk raised to second-highest level") is confusing people. The recall is a Class II recall of compounded tirzepatide from Apothecary Pharma; brand-name pens were not recalled. Our recall Short already ran on 10-20, so this has to be a long-form on how to check your pen, not a repeat.

Other good fits:
- Semaglutide's results across menopause stages (body-effect topics do well on Instagram).
- The handgrip-strength meta-analysis (muscle questions are a proven format).
- Wegovy pill vs shot.
- Stopping and regain (evergreen).

Calm, low-priority options:
- The new eye-condition (NAION) data from the AAO meeting. Scare framing has done poorly for us.
- Generic semaglutide in Canada. Only with strict no-sourcing rules.

Rejected: STAT's telehealth off-label addiction prescribing (as a how-to-get-it angle) and a gray-market 'retatrutide reconstitution' guide.

Sources checked: CBS/American Med Spa coverage, ScienceDaily/JAMA Netw Open, Sleep Review/NEJM, Medical Xpress (AAO), NPR/KFF on the Medicare Bridge, IQVIA/Dr. Reddy's on Canada, Moneytalks/MedShadow on the recall, the Zepbound KwikPen approval (January 2026, so it's not news).

candidates.topic: Retatrutide sold online: what CBS News' Oct 21 lab tests found, plus the JAMA Network Open Reddit study (Oct 2026)
candidates.angle: Lane B 'What's Actually Confirmed?' long-form: a calm, dated walk through what CBS's lab testing reported (Oct 21, 2026), what Penn's JAMA Network Open analysis of about 150,000 Reddit posts did and didn't show (increased appetite was the most-reported symptom, but the authors say they can't link it to the drug or confirm what people actually took), Lilly's lawsuits, and the FDA's status. Never name a seller and never explain buying or reconstitution. End by pointing viewers to a prescriber about approved options or the TRIUMPH trials.
candidates.predicted_peak: 2–6 days (CBS segment syndication plus the Lilly Q3 call on Oct 29)
candidates.why_now: CBS published its lab-test investigation on Oct 21. The JAMA Network Open Reddit study reached ScienceDaily and SciTechDaily on Oct 19–22. Gray-market Shorts are our strongest lane (median 102), and no Lane B long-form has been published yet.

evidence.signal: 'We bought and tested what was sold as an experimental weight loss drug. The lab results were "pretty terrifying."' (feed headline; the quote wasn't found in our search)
Summary of a CBS News investigation into unapproved retatrutide sales
Penn analysis of about 150,000 Reddit posts from about 40,000 users; increased appetite was the most-reported symptom; the authors' caveat: 'We can't say that retatrutide is causing these symptoms'
Lilly is cracking down, but some clinics still promote retatrutide

candidates.topic: Retatrutide for sleep apnea: phase 3 results (presented at Sleep Europe 2026, published in NEJM) in adults with obesity or overweight, with or without type 2 diabetes
candidates.angle: Lane C 'New GLP-1 Drug Decoded' first explainer with the new name first ('Retatrutide for Sleep Apnea: What the New Trials Found'). Explain the apnea-hypopnea index in plain words. Results: a drop of about 34 events per hour on 9 mg and about 32 on 12 mg, versus about 10 on placebo. Say clearly that it is investigational, not approved for sleep apnea, with a filing planned by Q1 2027. Name the common stomach side effects. Mention that tirzepatide is already FDA-approved for moderate-to-severe sleep apnea in adults with obesity, and include no switching advice.
candidates.why_now: The results came out at Sleep Europe 2026 with an NEJM paper. MedPage covered it Oct 21 ('Another Incretin Drug Proves Mettle in Sleep Apnea'). Health creators have barely covered it, and it fits the 48-hour Lane C window. It's also a body-effect topic, which does well on Instagram.

evidence.signal: Lilly's retatrutide reduced sleep apnea severity in phase 3
Two phase 3 trials (TRIUMPH-1-OSA and a companion trial) presented at #SleepEurope2026: greater apnea-hypopnea index reductions than placebo
'Another Incretin Drug Proves Mettle in Sleep Apnea'
Review of tirzepatide for sleep apnea, for approved-drug context

candidates.topic: Were Mounjaro and Zepbound recalled? No. The Class II recall covers compounded tirzepatide from Apothecary Pharma (22 lots), not Lilly's pens
candidates.angle: Myth correction plus Lane B: 'Compounded Tirzepatide Recall: Is Your Pen Affected?' Quote the FDA notice word for word: the recall began Sept 24, was classified Class II on Oct 10, and the reason is 'lack of assurance of sterility'. Clear up the confusion from headlines like 'Mounjaro, Zepbound ingredient risk raised'. Show how to tell a brand pen from a compounded vial, and send viewers to their pharmacist or prescriber. Never name sellers. Our 10-20 recall Short already covered this, so make it a long-form about checking your pen, not a repeat.
candidates.why_now: Between Oct 20 and 22, USA Today, the LA Times, Fox Business, the Boston Globe, Good Housekeeping and The Independent all ran the story. The MassLive headline implies the brand-name products are affected, which leaves lots of confused searchers.

evidence.signal: Confusing headline: 'GLP-1 recall: Mounjaro, Zepbound ingredient risk raised to second-highest level'
Recall started Sept 24, classified Class II on Oct 10; FDA warning letter in December 2025
The recall covers 22 lots, with expiry dates through November 2026
Roundup of FDA recalls and warning letters on compounded semaglutide and tirzepatide

candidates.topic: Does Medicare cover Wegovy or Zepbound? The Medicare GLP-1 Bridge's $50 copay (July 2026 to Dec 2027) during open enrollment, Oct 15 to Dec 7
candidates.angle: Lane A explainer: 'Does Medicare Cover Wegovy or Zepbound? The $50 Bridge Explained.' Cover who qualifies (Part D enrollment plus weight and health criteria, as CMS sets them), which products are included (Wegovy pill and injection, Zepbound KwikPen, Foundayo), when it ends, and the questions to ask your plan and prescriber. No ads and no telehealth sellers. Cite CMS, NPR and KFF Health News with dates.
candidates.why_now: ABC7 covered the Bridge on Oct 22. Open enrollment is live, so older US viewers are searching for coverage, and they pay the highest ad rates. Novo's 2027 price cuts (seen in 2 earlier snapshots) add a second hook.

evidence.signal: Some Medicare beneficiaries can get obesity drugs for $50 a month
A new Medicare option for weight loss drugs: what older Americans should know
Medicare GLP-1 Bridge program coverage

candidates.topic: Thanksgiving and holiday meals on tirzepatide or semaglutide: smaller plates, protein first, easier on the stomach
candidates.angle: Lane A 'Life on GLP-1': 'What to Eat at Thanksgiving on Tirzepatide or Semaglutide.' Cover the practical points: protein and vegetables first, smaller portions, slower eating, and why rich, fatty meals can worsen nausea. Use UC Davis Health and the dietitian guidance from The Conversation. Absolutely no extreme-diet or 'skip the meal' messaging, and keep a warm, non-judgmental tone. Shorts can take one body-effect question each ('Why does a big holiday meal feel worse on tirzepatide?').
candidates.predicted_peak: Nov 15–27 (publish by Nov 5 to build search history)
candidates.why_now: UC Davis Health published its holiday-meals guide on Oct 20. Seasonal US search demand climbs from early November. It refreshes the 'what to eat' topic we've seen twice in earlier snapshots (The Conversation, Oct 20).

evidence.signal: How to enjoy holiday meals while taking a GLP-1 weight loss medication
Started a GLP-1 drug like Ozempic or Mounjaro? What you need to know about nutrition
Rapid review of protein intake and resistance training

candidates.topic: Does semaglutide work after menopause? Wegovy results by menopause stage, plus the Mayo cohort of semaglutide with and without hormone therapy
candidates.angle: Body-effect explainer for women 45–65. In Novo's analysis by menopause stage, the 7.2 mg dose gave about 20–23% average weight loss at 72 weeks, consistent across stages. In the Mayo retrospective cohort, women on semaglutide plus menopausal hormone therapy lost about 16% at 12 months versus about 12% without it. That result is observational ('linked to'), not proof that hormone therapy boosts semaglutide. No advice to start hormone therapy; talk to your clinician.
candidates.why_now: MedicalNewsToday covered it Oct 21 and Bioengineer.org on Oct 20, around the Menopause Society meeting. Novo's menopause-stage data are new too. The audience fit is huge (women 45–65 in the US, UK, Canada and Australia), and body-effect topics do well on Instagram.

evidence.signal: Menopause: hormone therapy plus Wegovy linked to more weight loss
Wegovy weight-loss results consistent across menopause stages
Wegovy benefits may extend beyond weight loss in menopausal women

candidates.topic: Does semaglutide make you weaker? New meta-analysis of handgrip strength (Diabetes Obes Metab, Oct 19)
candidates.angle: Muscle outcome question (a proven Short format): what grip strength showed in the trials, and why strength matters more than lean-mass numbers. Pair it with the Nutrients review of protein and resistance training for practical, non-prescriptive habits. Never a '3 ways' list.
candidates.why_now: The meta-analysis is 3 days old and has seen 2 snapshots in a row with steady momentum. Muscle-question Shorts got 101 and 131 views, and almost no creators have covered this paper yet.

evidence.signal: Systematic review and meta-analysis of handgrip strength after semaglutide
Protein intake and resistance training across clinical populations

candidates.topic: Wegovy pill vs Wegovy shot: what's the difference? (oral semaglutide vs injection, Oct 2026)
candidates.angle: Lane A search-question long-form: how the pill works (daily, with fasting rules taken from the label), how weight loss compared in the trials, side effects, and why switching is a conversation for your prescriber, never DIY. Add the orforglipron (Foundayo) pill for context. Keep it calm and confirmed, and say 'don't switch on your own'.
keywords: is the wegovy pill as good as the shot
candidates.predicted_peak: ongoing; spikes with the France launch and the Novo Q3 results in early November
candidates.why_now: The France launch (Oct 21), Men's Journal's piece on switching (Oct 20), the Yahoo doctor explainer, the OMICS review (Oct 20) and Amazon Pharmacy listing news all point the same way. Search demand is high, but our pill-vs-shot long-form got only 9 views, so it must use the exact search phrase and add new switching data.

evidence.signal: Oral versus injectable incretin therapies: orforglipron, semaglutide, tirzepatide
Wegovy users switched to a daily pill
Novo to launch the Wegovy pill in France without reimbursement

candidates.topic: What happens when you stop semaglutide or tirzepatide? Regain data plus a new real-world persistence study (Diabetes Obes Metab, Oct 19)
candidates.angle: Lane A evergreen: what SURMOUNT-4 and the STEP 1 extension showed, plus the new US data on how starting habits relate to stopping early and to 1-year persistence. Frame it as 'why people stop and what helps them keep results'. No stopping or switching advice; decisions belong with the prescriber.
keywords: what happens when you stop ozempic
do you regain weight after wegovy
candidates.predicted_peak: evergreen; New Year refresh in January
candidates.why_now: It has appeared in 3 snapshots in a row (68, 66, 68). The new DOM persistence paper gives a fresh fact, and it's one of the playbook's named Lane A titles.

evidence.signal: Real-world semaglutide initiation behaviours and 1-year persistence
Treatment patterns before and after a tirzepatide price rise in more than 1 million UK self-payers

candidates.topic: Does semaglutide reduce drinking? What the trials show, as STAT reports telehealth companies prescribing GLP-1s off-label for addiction (Oct 22)
candidates.angle: Evidence-first explainer of the small randomized trials in alcohol use disorder, the Addictive Behaviors review and the ongoing VA trial, with clear 'early research, not approved for this' framing. Discuss off-label telehealth prescribing only as news context: no sources, no how-to. Optional add-on: what's known about GLP-1s and cannabis use (LiveNOW Fox).
candidates.why_now: STAT's Oct 22 story, the Medical Economics item 'semaglutide cuts heavy drinking', the Fox cannabis explainer and the BMJ crime-trial news (Oct 20) all hit this week, across several source types.

evidence.signal: Telehealth leapfrogs FDA approval with off-label GLP-1 prescriptions for addiction
Review of semaglutide for alcohol use disorder
US trial will test semaglutide and criminality

candidates.topic: Semaglutide and sudden vision loss (NAION): new AAO 2026 data on second-eye events in people who already had NAION
candidates.angle: Calm 'what's confirmed' framing, not scare framing. A retrospective database study (1,440 GLP-1 users vs 20,713 non-users, all of whom already had NAION) found more second-eye events within 6 months: 69.5% vs 52% of events. It is observational, and HbA1c was higher in users. Put it next to the EMA safety committee (PRAC) label wording (very rare). Tell people to get urgent care for sudden vision changes and not to stop medicines on their own.
candidates.why_now: The AAO meeting (Medical Xpress, Oct 21) and the Medical Economics item ('Wegovy may pose higher eye-stroke risk', Oct 22) are both new. But scare-framed eye topics got 34 views for us, so this is a filler only.

evidence.signal: AAO: sequential NAION occurs earlier with GLP-1 exposure
Semaglutide, diabetic retinopathy and NAION cohort

candidates.topic: Is there generic Ozempic? Generic semaglutide in Canada (Health Canada approval April 2026) and what IQVIA's Oct 2026 data show
candidates.angle: A Canada-focused explainer: what 'generic semaglutide' means, that Health Canada approved Dr. Reddy's version on Apr 28, 2026, and why US status differs. Strict rules: no cross-border buying, no sellers, no telehealth brands. Send viewers to their prescriber or pharmacist.
candidates.why_now: IQVIA published 'The Genericization of Semaglutide in Canada' on Oct 20, and it touches Canadian viewers' wallets directly. US viewers also search for 'generic Ozempic' all the time.

evidence.signal: Genericization of semaglutide in Canada
Dr. Reddy's launches generic semaglutide injection in Canada

candidates.topic: Why does weight loss plateau on tirzepatide or semaglutide? With Medscape's Oct 20 question about whether retatrutide could break a plateau
candidates.angle: Lane A: explain the plateau the trials show (weight levels off at around 60–72 weeks), why it's expected biology and not failure, and the habits that protect muscle. Mention retatrutide only as investigational research, with no switching advice.
keywords: why did I stop losing weight on mounjaro
candidates.why_now: Medscape published on Oct 20, and the Detroit News ran a 'one-size-fits-all' piece. The spread of results in STEP 1 and SURMOUNT-1 appeared in an earlier snapshot. Plateau is a top search question among our viewers.

evidence.signal: Could retatrutide break a GLP-1 weight-loss plateau?

candidates.topic: Can GLP-1 medicines lower clot and heart-rhythm risk? Medscape on atrial fibrillation (AF) and diabetes (Oct 22), plus an Int J Cardiol cohort on new AF in adults with obesity and chronic kidney disease
candidates.angle: Body-effect Short in the 'benefits beyond weight' pillar. Keep it strictly 'linked to', since both studies are observational. State each population exactly.
candidates.why_now: A new Medscape piece (Oct 22) and a new Int J Cardiol cohort (Oct 17). Few creators cover it, but search demand is modest.

evidence.signal: GLP-1 RAs may cut clot risk in AF and diabetes
GLP-1 RA therapy and new AF in adults with obesity and chronic kidney disease, without diabetes

candidates.topic: GLP-1 medicines and sperm health: Loma Linda explainer (Oct 21)
candidates.angle: Possible body-effect Short on men's fertility, but only if the underlying study can be verified. The evidence is early and mixed, so frame it as 'what we know and don't know'.
candidates.why_now: A single university news item; no corroborating source yet.

evidence.signal: The surprising link between GLP-1 medications and sperm health

candidates.topic: REJECT: retatrutide 'reference vial' reconstitution guide (Apopka Voice, Oct 20), and 'how to get GLP-1s off-label for addiction through telehealth'
candidates.angle: Do not cover. These are how-to and sourcing guides for unapproved or gray-market use, which breaks our guardrails on research chemicals, self-titration and no-prescription sources.
candidates.why_now: Listed only so downstream agents don't pick these up.

evidence.signal: Technical guide for retatrutide 'reference vials'
